input: Compile a reading list on behavioral economics

gold.taskTitle: Compile a reading list on behavioral economics
gold.taskDescription: Build a curated reading list focused on behavioral economics, tailored to the user's background, purpose, and preferences.

questions.title: What is your current knowledge level in this subject?
questions.description: Understand whether the user is a complete beginner, has some familiarity, or is already knowledgeable in behavioral economics.

questions.title: What is your main reason for exploring this topic?
questions.description: Identify the user's core motivation, such as academic study, professional application, personal curiosity, or a specific project.

questions.title: How many titles should the list include?
questions.description: Determine the desired size of the reading list so it is neither too short nor overwhelming.

questions.title: Which formats do you prefer: books, papers, or articles?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants full-length books, academic journal papers, long-form articles, or a mix.

questions.title: Is there a specific sub-topic you want prioritized?
questions.description: Identify any focused area within behavioral economics the user cares most about, such as decision-making, nudge theory, finance, or consumer behavior.

questions.title: Do you need resources that are freely available online?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user has access to paid books or academic databases, or requires only free, openly accessible resources.

questions.title: What is your target timeline to work through this list?
questions.description: Understand how much time the user plans to dedicate, which affects how many and how dense the recommended readings should be.
